items.criterion: F-DUR Runtime is 75 seconds (±0.1 s), the runtime the brief committed to.
items.why: brief mandates a single specific runtime. A loose tolerance invites padding.
items.check: `ffprobe -show_entries format=duration` → |d − 75| ≤ 0.1.

items.criterion: F-RES Video is delivered at 1920×1080, the horizontal YouTube frame the brief asked for.
items.why: brief names 1920 × 1080 explicitly. Vertical-upscale is a platform-mismatch failure.
items.check: `ffprobe -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height` → width == 1920, height == 1080.

items.criterion: F-ASPECT Display aspect ratio is 16:9 with no pillarboxing, letterboxing, or vertical content centred on black bars.
items.why: a 1920 × 1080 file with 9:16 content in a black-bar frame passes F-02 but defeats the platform choice. Catch it.
items.check: deterministic. `ffprobe` width/height ratio = 16:9 AND opus-vision sampled frames show no black-bar sidebars consuming more than 5% of horizontal extent.

items.criterion: F-AUDIO-PRESENT The file carries an audio stream with audible content; a silent export of a stand-up reel is not a deliverable.
items.why: trivially important; trivially catchable.
items.check: `ffprobe -show_streams` has an audio stream AND librosa RMS of full audio > −60 dBFS.

items.criterion: F-CODEC-SANE Video codec is H.264 or H.265 and audio codec is AAC or Opus, so the file plays on YouTube without re-encode surprises.
items.why: esoteric codecs (AV1 without --cpu-used tuning, ProRes, uncompressed) aren't a "deliverable" for YouTube.
items.check: `ffprobe -show_streams` codec_name ∈ {h264, hevc, h265} for video AND codec_name ∈ {aac, opus} for audio.

items.criterion: V-TITLECARD-CAP The end-title / Dry Bar card at the close occupies at most 3 seconds of the reel's runtime, in line with the brief's "a second or two, not a dragged-out pad."
items.why: anti-padding. Content density trades directly against title-card hold time, and the brief said a "second or two."
items.check: opus-vision over last 6 s at 1 fps; identify the contiguous end-card window (frames without speaker silhouette + mic on stand, or frames showing the Dry Bar app-promo layout). Pass iff that window ≤ 3 s.

items.criterion: V-CAPTIONS-PRESENT Burned-in English captions are visible during every stretch of spoken audio in the reel; only music-only beats and the end-title card are exempt.
items.why: brief explicitly asks for burned-in captions so a muted scroller can land the jokes. The whole deliverable premise assumes they're there.
items.check: gemini-video samples the reel at 1 fps; for each frame with non-silent speaker audio (RMS > −40 dBFS), pass iff visible on-screen text overlay is present.

items.criterion: V-CAPTIONS-SYNC-STRICT The on-screen caption matches the spoken word at every moment (within roughly a third of a second), and no caption line carries over from a prior clip after a cut. A muted viewer reading captions hears, in their head, the word Robert is actually saying.
items.why: the single most caption-craft-critical item. A caption that's close but half-a-beat off is worse than no caption because it actively misinforms the muted viewer.
items.check: gemini-video samples ≥ 5 evenly-spaced moments in the content body; at each, compare the on-screen caption against the concurrent audible word; pass iff paraphrase-OK, ≤ 3 words of drift, ≤ 0.3 s temporal drift at EVERY sampled moment AND no post-cut caption carryover.

items.criterion: V-CAPTIONS-LEGIBLE Captions are legible: large enough to read on a phone, high-contrast against the brick-wall set, and not clipped at the edge of the frame.
items.why: the muted-scroller use case dies the moment captions drop below readability. A visual-only check; no audio needed.
items.check: opus-vision samples repurposed cut at 1 fps; pass iff ≥ 90 % of frames with captions meet font-size (≥ 40 px body at 1080p), contrast (≥ 4.5:1 luminance ratio vs local background), and safe-area (no text clipped).

items.criterion: V-THESIS-VISUALLY-REINFORCED When Robert delivers his persona-thesis line ("I'm Robert Mack and I kill birds," or his "my brain is flexibleer than that" self-ID), the camera is on him chest-up on the Dry Bar stage — not on the end-title card and not on a wide where audience silhouettes are the subject.
items.why: the thesis line's job is done by Robert on camera, not by a caption over a blank plate. If the reel lets an editing beat steal the frame at the exact moment the thesis lands, the character doesn't land.
items.check: gemini-video finds the moment the repurposed cut audio carries the thesis sentence; pass iff during that moment ± 1 s the frame shows the speaker's face clearly (chest-up, face centered, not on an end-card or a wide-with-audience-as-subject).

items.criterion: V-NO-VISUAL-FABRICATION Every image in the reel is from the source footage. No stock B-roll under the bird/polar-bear/Panama-Canal beats, no illustrated maps, no motion-graphic inserts. The reel is Robert on stage, full stop.
items.why: the source has no B-roll, no cutaways, no demos. Any visual that isn't Robert on the Dry Bar stage is fabricated and changes what the reel is.
items.check: opus-vision samples repurposed cut at 1 fps; for each frame, require either (a) a speaker-on-stage shot matching source pHash within threshold 12, or (b) a recognizable Dry Bar title-card / end-card frame. Pass iff all sampled frames match one of those two categories.

items.criterion: V-FRAMING-CONSISTENT The reel keeps Robert's full face in frame and the mic stand visible — no aggressive vertical-style reframe that crops his forehead or slices the mic out of the shot.
items.why: a reframe that crops forehead-to-mouth-only to "fit vertical" even in a 16:9 export reads as a platform-mismatch artifact. The brief committed to horizontal.
items.check: opus-vision samples repurposed cut at 1 fps; pass iff ≥ 80 % of content-body frames show the speaker's full face (forehead to chin) inside the frame AND the microphone stand is visible in at least one frame of each speaker clip.

items.criterion: N-THESIS Robert's persona-thesis line — "I'm Robert Mack and I kill birds," or its callback "I do because I kill birds" — is audibly in the reel in his own voice, and lands inside the first 30 seconds or the last 15 seconds. This is the single sentence that names the character.
items.why: the line that does all the character-framing work for a cold viewer. Every other bit reads wrong without it.
items.check: whisper the repurposed cut audio; pass iff the string "I'm Robert Mack and I kill birds" (≤ 3 words of drift) OR the string "I do because I kill birds" is substring-findable in the repurposed cut transcript AND its timestamp is within [0, 30] s or [runtime − 15, runtime] s of the reel.

items.criterion: N-COLD-VIEWER-COMPREHENSION A viewer who has never seen the source can, after one watch, (a) state the persona — a confidently-wrong "problem thinker" who proposes absurd solutions to large public problems; (b) name at least two specific bits from the reel (Shorter Border Order / Panama Canal, Remove the Fire, Hottest-Month-Ever, HB2 Peepee Lady Style, Pass-holes, White Bears Can't Jump, Pythagorean cheetah); and (c) recognize where the reel lands (thesis restated, signoff, callback).
items.why: baseline comprehension. The whole point of an insight reel is that it IS a standalone persuasion, not a trailer for the 42-minute set.
items.check: opus-vision given repurpose frames at 1 fps + full repurpose transcript, plus gemini-video for audio-concurrent reads; judge answers (a) persona-statable? (b) at least two of the seven named bits recoverable? (c) closing beat recoverable? Pass iff all three yes.

items.criterion: N-BIT-SUPPORT-WITH-NAMED-DETAIL At least two of the bits in the reel arrive with their specific named detail — the thing that makes the bit Mack's rather than a generic premise. A specific number ("2,000-mile dotted line," "one 5,000th of a mile"), a specific named referent ("Panama Canal, short and very secure, what with all those locks," "Robert Plant of the Led Zeppelins," "Pythagorean theorem"), a persona-catchphrase tag ("I kill birds," "I happen to know a lot of stuff," "I'm not the best driver"), or an escalating list / callback (the HB2 productivity list, the cheetah Pythagorean math). A bit paired with a vague "and then it's funny" beat does NOT count.
items.why: a bit without its specific detail reads as a premise without a punchline. The detail is what separates a Mack reel from a generic-comedian reel.
items.check: opus-vision with repurpose frames at 1 fps + repurpose transcript; for each audible bit, map to its adjacent (within ± 5 s) detail beat; pass iff ≥ 2 bits are paired with a named detail of type (a)-(d).

items.criterion: N-OPENS-ON-SUBSTANCE The first 5 seconds carry Robert's voice on a line that tells the scroller what kind of person they're watching — a persona-line, a landed punchline, a signature quote. Housekeeping intros, slow fades from black, logo-only Dry Bar holds, and music-only cold-opens are not acceptable openers.
items.why: brief says "open on something that earns the next fifteen seconds." A scroller decides in three seconds. The first five must carry voice + character.
items.check: opus-vision + repurpose whisper transcript; pass iff the first 5 s of content has Robert's voice audible AND at least one identifiable persona-cue (a persona-catchphrase, a landed punchline, a signature quote from moments) is present in those 5 s.

items.criterion: N-NO-FABRICATION Every line in the reel keeps its load-bearing setup. Three risk moments: (i) the "white bears can't jump" tag must arrive with the "polar bears evolved in the Arctic and there are no trees" setup within the prior 10 s; (ii) "Come on people, follow the money" or "Sainara, China" from the Chinese-New-Year/gluten bit must arrive with its persona-frame ("I'm kind of opposed [to China] right now" or a Mack persona-catchphrase) within 15 s; (iii) "peepee lady style" or the HB2 productivity capper must arrive with either the "North Carolina House Bill 2" framing OR the "birth certificate" / "federale under the stall" setup within the prior 15 s. Stripped of setup, these lines invert from satire into endorsement.
items.why: these three lines invert meaning when stripped of setup. Satire becomes endorsement. A reel that lifts them without their scaffolding fabricates a POV Robert did not perform.
items.check: repurpose whisper transcript is scanned for each of the three risk-moment strings; for each hit, the preceding 10-15 s of repurpose transcript is checked for the required setup sentence (with paraphrase tolerance ≤ 20 %). Pass iff every risk-moment hit has its required setup; auto-pass iff no risk-moment hits appear in the reel.

items.criterion: N-CLOSES-ON-LANDING The last 10 seconds of the content body (before the end-title card) land on a Mack beat — a landed punchline, a persona-callback, a restated thesis, or a signoff in Robert's voice. Not acceptable: a slow fade into the end card with no spoken content, a mid-sentence truncation, or a Dry Bar logo-only card occupying that window.
items.why: brief says close on a Dry Bar card "a second or two, not a dragged-out pad." A reel that lets the card steal the last ten seconds has no ending.
items.check: opus-vision + repurpose transcript; locate the end-title window (via V-TITLECARD-CAP check); pass iff the 10 seconds immediately preceding that window contain Robert-voice audio AND end on a complete-sentence landing (no mid-word or mid-clause truncation).

items.criterion: N-PERSONA-SUSTAINED The reel stays inside Robert's performed persona from the first audible frame through the final landing. No "here's a clip from…" framing voiceover, no meta caption explaining the bit, no non-Mack narrator interrupting the set. The scroller's experience is Robert performing, uninterrupted.
items.why: the character is the product. A framing device that breaks the fourth wall (even in Mack's own voice, if the line is lifted out of the set context as a narration) collapses the character-frame that N-01 and N-02 depend on.
items.check: gemini-video reviews the reel end-to-end; pass iff no frame contains (a) a non-speaker voice-over over the picture, OR (b) a caption/title-card layered on top of the picture that reframes what we're watching as a clip-of ("here's Robert doing…", "in this bit, Robert says…"), OR (c) a Mack-voice line placed as narration over a non-stage plate.

items.criterion: S-SEAM-QUALITY Cuts in the repurposed cut land at natural sentence/word boundaries (and natural laugh-break boundaries — punchlines must be allowed to land), not mid-sentence or mid-word or mid-laugh. The repurposed cut reads as a clean assembly, not a chopped one.
items.why: the reel is heavily cut by nature. Sloppy seams undermine the reel's authority more than a bad visual cut.
items.check: gemini-audio on repurpose audio only; pass iff there are no audibly jarring seam artifacts: no > 6 dB loudness jumps at cut points, consistent room-tone, no audible clicks or pumps at seams.

items.criterion: P4-CAPTIONS-ASYNC Somewhere in the reel, the caption on screen disagrees with what Robert is audibly saying — the caption drifts more than half a second from the audio, persists across a cut and now contradicts the new clip, or shows text Robert is not actually saying. A muted viewer reading captions must never, at any moment, be misinformed about what Robert just said.
items.why: worst-case caption failure: active misinformation for the muted-scroller audience the brief was written for. Weight is steep because the whole caption premise collapses if a single visible line says the wrong thing.
items.check: gemini-video examines every speaker-clip transition and every continuous caption line; fire iff any caption line satisfies (a) OR (b) OR (c).

items.criterion: P4-CAPTIONS-UNREADABLE Captions are present but functionally unreadable — too small to read on a phone, dark-on-dark for multi-second stretches, or clipped off the edge of the frame.
items.why: less severe than ASYNC (the viewer gets NO info rather than WRONG info), but still defeats the brief's core muted-scroller use case. Moderate weight.
items.check: opus-vision samples repurposed cut at ≥ 10 evenly-spaced moments; for each, check caption font-size (< 30 px body → illegible), contrast (< 3:1 luminance ratio vs local background → dark-on-dark), and safe-area (text clipped off-edge → clipped). Fire iff ≥ 2 samples flagged illegible.
